messages:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for requests routed to us-west1 gateway (ingress-gw-*) starting ~T-3m. Error mix: 502/504/503. 95th latency > 2s. Rolling error budget burn. Automated retry disabled for affected routes.

eric: Ack. I'm on call, investigating. Pinging infra and routing teams. Any recent deploys to gateway cluster?

maria: Not seeing deploys in us-west infra in last 30m. I'm pulling gateway health and upstream error rates now.

sam: I can check proxy tail logs and LB metrics. If it's backend saturation or NLB health, we should see connection resets on the gateway pods.

ops-bot: Attached recent NGINX error tail (sample):
```
2025-09-13T14:01:22Z error upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client=10.1.4.22, server_name=api.redwood-inference.com, request="POST /v1/generate"
2025-09-13T14:02:05Z 504 gateway timeout, upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
```

karen: Customer-impact check: PagerDuty shows pages from two customers with high error rates. CS notified. We should estimate what percentage of traffic is affected and for which customers (hosted vs dedicated).

maria: Quick overview: traffic to us-west1 routes is ~12% of global production. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream for models xlarge-1 and xlarge-2. Dedicated customers pinned to us-west1 see errors; hosted customers on multi-region routing fall back sometimes but see increased latency and occasional 5xx.

sam: Hypothesis: upsteam model-serving pool in us-west1 is overloaded/evicted due to node OOMs or noisy tenant. Node metrics show GPU mem pressure spikes and kube-scheduler evictions on pool-2-gpu.*

eric: Can we fail over traffic for non-pinned routes to us-east1 as an emergency mitigation? What's the risk for users with region pinning?

lia: We have weighted routing by policy. For non-pinned traffic we can shift traffic by updating traffic-split: route weight 80->us-east1. Doing a gradual 20% step every 60s should be safe. For pinned tenants we'll need to contact account owners.

maria: I can start the traffic-split change. Command:
```bash
redwood route update --route api-prod --weights us-west1=20,us-east1=80 --reason "emergency failover due to us-west1 5xx"
```
I'll hold off until eric gives go.

eric: Go ahead. Proceed with 20% -> 40% if metrics still bad. Keep me posted.

maria: Doing first 20% shift now.

ops-bot: Route update applied: us-west1=20, us-east1=80. Monitoring for 2m.

maria: Early signs: 5xx rate for us-west1 traffic decreased marginally; overall user-facing 5xx count dropping ~30%. Latency on us-east1 increased slightly but within SLOs.

sam: Investigating model-serving pool logs. Found repeated OOM kill traces and one node daemon reporting GPU driver crash:
```
Sep 13 14:03:10 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, Graphics Exception: Reason: 0x00000040
kubectl describe pod model-serve-xyz
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilled  2m  kubelet  Container killed due to out of memory
```

lia: If nodes are unstable, we should cordon and drain affected nodes to avoid noisy neighbor impact and scale up a hot spare pool in us-west1. But that might be slower than routing shift.

karen: CS update: Pinned dedicated customers in us-west1 being contacted. Status page draft: short blurb about elevated errors in us-west1, mitigation in progress, link to status. Please review: "We are seeing elevated error rates and timeouts for us-west1. We have shifted the majority of non-pinned traffic to us-east1 as a mitigation while we investigate. Some dedicated customers in us-west1 may still see errors. Engineers are actively debugging."

eric: Approve status blurb. Add expected next update in 30 minutes and a note that it's an active incident with potential customer impact for pinned deployments.

maria: Next actions: 1) continue routing shift steps if errors persist 2) cordon/drain unhealthy nodes 3) scale up replacement nodes in us-west1 4) if GPU driver crash widespread, trigger rolling restart of the model-serving pool with maxUnavailable=1.

sam: I'm working on a hotfix: adjust container ulimits and prevent bursty batch jobs from grabbing >80% GPU memory. Preparing a canary patch for one deployment.

eric: Handing off to maria for next 30m. I'm switching to incident commander role for escalation/interface with support. Maria, ping me if traffic shift doesn't restore 90% of baseline or if customer P0s escalate.

maria: Taking on-call. I'll post updates every 5-10m or on state changes. First checkpoint in 10m.

ops-bot: Automated observation: after weight change, aggregate 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% -> 1.6% within 180s. Latency 95th increased on us-east1 by 120ms.

lia: Recommendation: continue to 40% if steady. Also request infra to pre-warm new nodes (image+drivers) to reduce time-to-scale.

sam: Canary applied to one model-serving deployment with memory hardening. Watching for regressions.

karen: CS: two customers reported transient errors but most recovered after routing change. We'll keep them updated as you progress.

maria: Applying second weight step to us-east1 (us-west1=0, us-east1=100) for non-pinned routes to stop most errors while we fix nodes.

ops-bot: Route update applied: us-west1=0, us-east1=100 for non-pinned. Monitoring.

maria: After full shift, aggregate 5xx back to baseline ~0.2%. Pinned dedicated tenants still affected; we're scheduling 1:1 account callbacks.

eric: Good. Next: infra to replace/repair GPU nodes, ops to run health checks and perform rolling restart when nodes stable. Also create a follow-up action item for longer-term: auto-eviction policies and better noisy-tenant isolation.

maria: I'll create incident ticket with RCA checklist and link to runbook steps taken. Will include timeline and customer list.

sam: Noted a potential bug in container runtime that allows jobs to exceed requested memory under load; will open a GitHub issue and link to incident.

eric: Thanks all. Handing back to incident rotation — incident remains open. Maria, continue as primary on-call. I'll stay on the bridge for customer escalations.

maria: Update in 20m or on major state change. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident note added to ticket: "us-west1 gateway - elevated 5xx due to GPU node instability; mitigation: traffic failover to us-east1 for non-pinned, cordon/drain and scale-up of replacement nodes, canary container limit fixes."

karen: Posting to status page now. Will add link to incident ticket and customer notifications.

maria: (closing interim) We have stable mitigation in place. Leaving incident open for cleanup and RCA.
